title: SCRAP YARD '95
premise: A retro-styled scrapyard crash toy where the player drops odd junk items into a neon wreck lot and drags them together to make them collide, burst apart, and clear the field.
interaction_model: Single-screen direct manipulation via mouse or touch; the player starts the session, spawns junk, drags items around the canvas, releases them to slide, and clears the lot with a reset button.
objective: Create chaotic, satisfying wrecks by slamming spawned scrap pieces into each other and enjoying the resulting explosions, splashes, sounds, and visual feedback.
progression: Open-ended sandbox progression with no levels or win state; momentum comes from repeatedly spawning more junk, creating denser collision opportunities, and occasionally clearing the lot to start fresh.
theme: 1990s scrapyard arcade spectacle with neon industrial styling, CRT overlays, hazard-strip visuals, and goofy anthropomorphic junk objects.
mood: Playful, noisy, chaotic, tactile, arcade-like, and lightly comedic.
likely_audience: Casual players, kids, and anyone who enjoys toy-like physics sandboxes, quick audiovisual feedback, and low-pressure browser interactions.
confidence_notes: High confidence that this is a single-screen drag-to-crash sandbox with no structured victory condition.
High confidence that the main appeal is audiovisual collision spectacle rather than optimization or strategy.
Moderate confidence that the fiction suggests a magnet scrapyard fantasy, though the implemented mechanics are simpler direct dragging rather than an actual magnet tool.
Moderate confidence that combo messaging is flavor feedback more than a fully developed scoring system.
recreation_prompt: Recreate a browser game called "SCRAP YARD '95" as a fullscreen single-screen arcade sandbox with a retro CRT scrapyard presentation. The player begins on a stylish start panel, then enters a neon industrial wreck lot rendered on an HTML5 canvas. Populate the yard with a small set of goofy scrap objects such as a bus, door, log, ball, milk carton, and pencil, each with distinct sizes, colors, and hand-drawn cartoon-like details. The core gameplay loop should be simple and tactile: tap or click a button to spawn random junk into the lot, grab any object directly with mouse or touch, drag it around freely, and release it so it glides with light momentum and friction in a top-down space. When two objects overlap closely enough, treat that as a destructive crash: remove both items, play a crunchy impact sound, and spawn a burst of particles, with milk cartons creating a whiter splash-like effect. Include a second button to clear the entire lot in one dramatic reset that explodes every remaining object at once. Show a live HUD counter for how many wrecks or items are currently active, and display short animated feedback badges for moments like big collisions, crowded junk buildup, or reset events. Use layered gradients, hazard-strip cues, scanlines, glowing rails, and bold arcade typography to sell a 1990s junkyard broadcast vibe. Add looping background music plus responsive spawn, drag, crash, and reset sounds. Keep the experience mobile-safe and immediate, with no levels, no fail state, and no deep progression beyond spawning more scrap, causing louder chaos, and enjoying the spectacle of repeated crash-and-clear play.
